title: TIME JUMP — 23:30 CST: Warning Expired, North End in the Dark

fields.scenarioTitle: Rain-Wrapped — Night Tornado Warning & Shelter Timing
fields.narration: It is now 23:30 CST, Friday, December 11, 2026. The tornado warning for northern Brennan County expired at 23:15. The tornado that crossed Pine Hollow and the southwest edge of Corwin has moved northeast and is out of the county. The PDS Tornado Watch remains in effect until 04:00. NWS Paducah says the trailing part of the line is weaker, but they are still watching it. Brennan Rural Electric Cooperative now reports about 6,800 members without power across the North zone. That includes all of Corwin, Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres. Cell sites in the north end lost commercial power at 22:58 and are running on battery. The 911 floor still has two telecommunicators and one supervisor, with nine calls holding and the number climbing. Fire district and Sheriff units are working their way into Corwin through downed trees and power lines, with no streetlights. Channel 6 is still on air from its basement backup set with one camera. Sirens N-07 and N-11 are still out. At 22:58 the Corwin Wax & Candle night lead called 911 to say people were sheltering in the offices and the east wall was shaking, then the line dropped, and callbacks have gone to voicemail since. No one knows yet how many people are hurt. Take two minutes to update your status, then we continue. THIS IS AN EXERCISE.
worldState: Clock is 23:30 CST, Friday, December 11, 2026.
Tornado Warning 0071 for northern Brennan County expired at 23:15. No tornado warning is in effect for any part of the county right now.
The PDS Tornado Watch remains in effect until 04:00. NWS Paducah is still watching the weaker trailing part of the line.
Brennan Rural Electric Cooperative: about 6,800 members without power in the North zone, including all of Corwin, Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres. No restoration estimate has been given.
North-end cell sites have been on battery since 22:58. Calls and texts in Corwin and the Clarks River parks may fail or arrive late.
911 overnight floor: two telecommunicators and one supervisor, with 9 calls holding and climbing.
Fire districts and Sheriff units are entering Corwin slowly. Roads are blocked by downed trees and power lines, and the streets are dark.
Channel 6 StormTeam is still on the basement backup set with one camera, no storm-track graphics and radar from a laptop.
Sirens N-07 (Pine Hollow) and N-11 (Clarks River bridge) are still out of service.
Corwin Wax & Candle's night lead called 911 at 22:58 from the offices, then the line dropped. Callbacks go to voicemail.
The number of injured, trapped or dead people is not known. No damage survey has started.
fields.facilitatorNote: Give the room two minutes for a round of status updates. Then ask the EM Director to state the EOC readiness level out loud and name an owner for each of these: the 911 call backlog, field command in Corwin, the communications gaps (cell sites on battery, power out in the North zone, Channel 6 on backup) and public messaging. Do not give any casualty figure. The open River Valley News 12 request and the locked-safe-room rumor are still unresolved.

instructorNote: This card moves the exercise from warning to response. Annex 3.1 calls for Level 3 on any tornado warning, a confirmed tornado or damage reports, so the EOC should already be at Level 3 or move there now with named owners. Watch whether anyone treats the expired warning as an all-clear while the PDS watch is still in effect, and whether the PIO waits for verified information before giving out any casualty numbers.
